strategy_objective_guidance:
- The supplied evaluator wrapper contains no scoring function, validity checks, test instances, return-format requirements, or use of `combined_score`; it only serializes calls to a hidden `evaluator.py` through a file lock and invokes its `evaluate(program_path)`. Therefore no scored terms, numerical weights, maxima, remaining lever, or term conflicts can be determined from the provided material.
- The only evaluator-visible hard condition evident here is that the submitted program must be loadable and must satisfy the hidden evaluator’s expected `search_algorithm(src, dsts, G, num_partitions)` interface. Runtime/concurrency behavior may matter because evaluation is serialized, but no runtime score or timeout is exposed.
- Complete problem-instance input appears to be available in a single call through `src`, all `dsts`, `G`, and `num_partitions`. This permits offline/batch optimization over the whole destination set and topology; a causal or streaming routing policy is not required by the visible interface.
- The nominal goal is minimizing broadcast transfer cost, but it is not safe to claim that the hidden evaluator rewards total path cost, bottleneck load, redundancy elimination, partition usage, latency, or any weighted combination. In particular, no assertion can be made that the highest evaluator score matches the best real cloud-transfer plan until hidden scoring is inspected.
- Largest remaining lever: obtain/read the hidden `/home/chenhui/efficient-evolve/benchmarks/ADRS/cloudcast/evaluator/evaluator.py` scoring logic or use evaluation outcomes to infer it. Without that, tuning toward nominal routing cost may optimize an unscored property and stall.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
EXAMPLES OF DIFFERENT approaches:
- [global directed Steiner/arborescence approximation] Build one shared multicast subgraph rooted at `src`, rather than independently routing to each destination; `networkx.algorithms.approximation.steiner_tree` applies only to undirected graphs, so use it only if topology semantics permit conversion, otherwise use directed shortest-path unions via `networkx.single_source_dijkstra`.
- [independent shortest-path baseline] Compute all destination routes from one source-search pass; `networkx.single_source_dijkstra`, `networkx.single_source_dijkstra_path`, and `networkx.single_source_dijkstra_path_length` directly reduce repeated path-search work while preserving nonnegative edge-cost semantics.
- [partition-aware load balancing] Treat `num_partitions` as divisible data units and assign each partition across alternative paths/subgraphs; `networkx.shortest_simple_paths` supplies candidate routes, while `scipy.optimize.linprog` can solve a fractional minimum-cost allocation if the hidden evaluator accepts a plan compatible with splitting.
- [min-cost flow formulation] Model broadcast replication and capacity/load constraints as flow only if replication semantics can be represented by the expected output; `networkx.min_cost_flow`, `networkx.network_simplex`, and `networkx.min_cost_flow_cost` provide mature exact flow solvers, but ordinary flow may overcharge shared prefixes and thus differs from multicast-tree cost.
- [cut/resilience-oriented topology selection] Identify shared bottlenecks and disjoint alternatives before assigning partitions; `networkx.minimum_edge_cut`, `networkx.edge_disjoint_paths`, and `networkx.node_disjoint_paths` support alternatives when the hidden score includes congestion, failures, or overlapping transfers.
- [exact small-instance optimization] For small destination counts, enumerate/DP over destination subsets or candidate route unions; use `itertools` plus `networkx` shortest-path primitives, reserving this family for cases where hidden evaluation favors true shared-edge cost over fast heuristics.
strategy_refine_guidance:
EXAMPLES OF REFINEMENT approaches:
- shortest-path union refinement; use the graph’s actual cost attribute consistently via `weight="cost"` or the evaluator-required edge-weight key, and explicitly handle directed versus undirected graph semantics.
- shared-prefix refinement; after forming candidate paths, prune non-terminal leaves with `networkx.algorithms.tree.branchings`/graph edge removal logic only when doing so preserves reachability from `src` to every `dst`.
- partition-allocation refinement; increase candidate-path budget from 1 to a small fixed `k` using `networkx.shortest_simple_paths`, then allocate integer partitions with rounding that preserves exactly `num_partitions`.
- flow refinement; set `scipy.optimize.linprog(method="highs")` feasibility tolerances and post-round only if output requires integral partition assignments; verify every destination remains served after rounding.
- performance refinement; perform one `networkx.single_source_dijkstra` search from `src` instead of one `shortest_path` call per destination when all routes use the same nonnegative edge weight.
- validity refinement; validate that every destination is reachable, every referenced edge exists in `G`, no path violates directionality, and returned partition counts/plan fields exactly match the hidden interface before pursuing nominal cost improvements.

strategies.title: [directed-steiner-dp] Exact small-terminal shared broadcast arborescence
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: directed-steiner-dp

Replacement scope: Replace the body of `search_algorithm`, specifically the independent per-destination Dijkstra loop, with a rooted directed Steiner dynamic program for small destination sets and the existing shortest-path construction only as an unreachable-instance fallback.

Compute budget: One deterministic DP solve; cap exact solving at 7 unique destinations, requiring at most `2^7` terminal subsets, no optimizer starts, and no iterative optimizer. Expected evaluation-time effect is moderate only for small graphs and destination sets; larger terminal sets use a bounded greedy fallback.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent minimizes every destination path independently, so it cannot intentionally choose a slightly longer route to one destination when that route reuses an expensive source-side transfer already needed by another destination. Compute `DP[mask][v]`, the minimum unique-edge cost of a directed subgraph rooted at `v` reaching all terminals in `mask`; combine disjoint terminal subsets at the same node, then relax those merged costs backward over incoming directed edges with multi-source Dijkstra. Reconstruct the resulting rooted edge set, derive a valid `src -> dst` path for each destination from that edge set, and assign the same valid broadcast tree paths to every partition. Preserve validity by excluding incoming edges to `src`, excluding self-loops, using only existing directed edges with finite numeric cost, and falling back to the current shortest paths if any destination is unreachable. Expected-gain check: this construction has the new ability to share an edge whose cost is paid once in the broadcast subgraph whereas the incumbent cannot represent that tradeoff; it should be retained only when the evaluator reports `total_cost < 1035.135735`, equivalently a score above `0.000965124516239` under the observed inverse-cost ranking.

strategies.title: [incremental-multicast-growth] Marginal-cost terminal attachment tree
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: incremental-multicast-growth

Replacement scope: Replace the current `for dst in dsts` routing phase with a bounded multi-order greedy multicast-tree constructor.

Compute budget: At most 8 deterministic destination orders: original order, reverse order, ascending and descending source shortest-path distance, plus one order beginning with each of up to four destinations. Each attachment performs one Dijkstra search with already-selected tree edges assigned zero marginal weight. No numerical optimizer iterations. Expected evaluation-time effect is at most eight times the present route-search phase.

Gain mechanism: Maintain a set of selected directed edges. For each next destination, find a route from `src` using edge weight zero for an already-selected edge and normal `cost` otherwise; add only the newly required edges. This optimizes the marginal cost of attaching a terminal to the growing broadcast topology rather than its standalone path cost. Score each completed candidate by the sum of unique selected edge costs and emit the lowest-cost candidate, with each destination represented by a directed source path contained in that candidate. It preserves hard validity because every recorded path is obtained from the directed graph, every edge reference is copied from `G`, every destination retains exactly `num_partitions` paths, and the independent shortest-path union remains the reachable fallback. Expected-gain check: the incumbent has no state representing an already-paid edge, while zero-marginal reuse explicitly adds that degree of freedom; the falsifiable acceptance threshold is evaluator `total_cost < 1035.135735`.

strategies.title: [union-local-reroute] Shared-edge local replacement refinement
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: union-local-reroute

Replacement scope: Replace only the path-selection portion after the initial single-source shortest-path tree is built; retain `BroadCastTopology` construction and partition serialization unchanged.

Compute budget: Start from one single-source Dijkstra tree, then perform at most two deterministic passes over destinations. Each destination receives at most one modified-weight Dijkstra search per pass, for no more than `2 * len(dsts)` local route attempts. Expected evaluation-time effect is small and bounded.

Gain mechanism: Form the unique-edge union of the initial shortest paths. For each destination in deterministic order, temporarily remove that destination’s current path contribution, set all remaining union edges to zero weight, and compute a replacement route. Commit the route only if the unique-edge union cost strictly decreases; otherwise preserve the old route. This is a local refinement of the actual broadcast subgraph rather than a repeat of independent shortest paths: it can replace a destination’s cheapest standalone path with a route that joins another branch earlier and eliminates a redundant paid edge. Each attempted replacement is directed and source-reachable, and committing only a strictly lower unique-edge union retains reachability and path-format validity; absent a finite replacement it keeps the initial shortest path. Expected-gain check: a successful committed replacement removes at least one positive-cost unique edge from the emitted union, a transformation unavailable to the incumbent’s independent routing loop, and is falsified unless the evaluator returns `total_cost < 1035.135735`.

strategies.title: [relay-hub-enumeration] Explicit common-relay broadcast candidate
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: relay-hub-enumeration  
Replacement scope: Replace the `elif len(unique_dsts) > 7:` greedy-only fallback in `search_algorithm` with a candidate comparison that includes bounded common-relay arborescences.  
Compute budget: At most 24 relay candidates, each requiring one source-to-relay path and at most one relay-to-destination shortest-path computation per destination; expected evaluation-time increase is modest and only applies when there are more than seven unique destinations.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent’s large-terminal fallback grows source-rooted paths in a few terminal orders, but does not explicitly search a topology where one inexpensive inter-cloud relay receives the data once and fans it out over a different provider/network. Enumerate reachable relay nodes ranked by `dist(src, relay)`, construct `path(src, relay) ∪ path(relay, dst)` for every destination, union the directed edges, and retain the candidate only when all destinations remain reachable. Compare this union-cost candidate against the incumbent tree and preserve the cheaper feasible graph. This explicitly exposes cross-network hub-and-spoke fanout that ordered source-path growth may miss. Hard validity is preserved by using only directed paths returned by Dijkstra on the filtered graph, copying only edges present in `G`, and retaining baseline paths for any unreachable destination. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless hidden evaluation reports `combined_score > 0.00161523997524`; the new explicit relay choice is absent from the incumbent’s bounded order construction and can strictly reduce its selected edge union when a low-cost fanout relay exists.

strategies.title: [branch-subtree-exchange] Exact local replacement of expensive multicast branche
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: branch-subtree-exchange  
Replacement scope: Replace the final selected-edge decision block after `_greedy_tree` with a bounded improvement phase operating on the currently selected directed tree.  
Compute budget: At most 12 branch candidates; for each candidate solve at most one exact directed-Steiner problem containing no more than seven affected terminals, with no iterative numerical optimization; expected evaluation-time increase is bounded and applies principally to destination sets larger than seven.  
Gain mechanism: Form a rooted predecessor tree from the selected union, identify branch roots whose descendants contain between two and seven requested destinations, remove that branch’s edges, and retain the remainder as the fixed broadcast backbone. For each removed branch, enumerate the existing backbone vertices that can reach the branch terminals as attachment candidates, solve an exact directed-Steiner subtree from each attachment root to the affected terminals, and splice the cheapest feasible subtree back into the backbone. This allows an expensive suffix of a greedy tree to reconnect through a different already-paid prefix or intermediate cloud, a local topology change unavailable to the incumbent because its greedy construction never revisits prior terminal attachments. Require reachability from `src` to every destination in the spliced graph before accepting it, and generate final paths only by directed shortest paths in that graph. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless evaluator output exceeds `0.00161523997524`; the falsifiable structural condition for improvement is that one selected branch has a strictly cheaper feasible attachment-and-subtree union than its current branch edge set, which the one-pass fallback does not test.

strategies.title: [terminal-cluster-core] Clustered exact multicast core with gateway composition
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: terminal-cluster-core  
Replacement scope: Replace `_greedy_tree` for terminal sets above the exact-DP limit with a deterministic clustered-core construction, while retaining `_greedy_tree` as a feasible fallback candidate.  
Compute budget: Build at most four deterministic terminal clusters and solve at most four exact subproblems of at most seven terminals each; enumerate at most eight source-reachable cluster gateway nodes per cluster; expected evaluation-time effect is bounded by 32 small exact solves plus shortest-path preprocessing.  
Gain mechanism: Compute source shortest paths and group destinations by their first non-source transit region, falling back to deterministic cost-nearest grouping when those paths do not share a first transit node. For each cluster, enumerate low-cost reachable gateways, construct a source-to-gateway prefix, and solve exact directed Steiner from that gateway to the cluster terminals. Union all cluster subgraphs and prune nonterminal leaves while preserving directed reachability. Unlike global ordered greedy growth, this creates separately optimized regional multicast subtrees whose prefixes may use different cloud networks and whose internal fanout is exact rather than dependent on a destination insertion order. Keep the original candidate if a cluster is infeasible or the composed union is not cheaper. Validity follows from filtered nonnegative directed edges, explicit source reachability checks, and fallback paths for malformed inputs. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless the evaluator returns a score above `0.00161523997524`; its new degree of freedom is independently chosen gateway-to-cluster exact fanout, which the incumbent’s single globally ordered source-rooted construction does not optimize as a subsystem.

strategies.title: [core-steiner-composition] Exact multicast core followed by marginal terminal at
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: core-steiner-composition
Replacement scope: Replace the `elif len(unique_dsts) > 7:` greedy-only fallback block in `search_algorithm`.
Compute budget: At most 12 deterministic core candidates; each core contains at most 7 terminals and uses the existing exact DP once; each remaining terminal is attached with one marginal-cost Dijkstra search. Expected evaluation-time effect: bounded increase over the current four-to-eight greedy order searches, with no exponential DP beyond 7 terminals.
Gain mechanism: The current large-terminal fallback commits to a purely sequential attachment order, so its early choices cannot form an exact shared trunk for a geographically coherent subset of destinations. Build deterministic cores by choosing each destination as a seed and adding its nearest terminals according to symmetric source-reachable shortest-path distance; solve the core exactly with `_directed_steiner_edges`, then attach every non-core destination using marginal edge cost zero on already selected edges. Also include a source-distance-nearest core and a source-distance-farthest core. Score every resulting union by `_edge_union_cost` and retain the best valid candidate against the incumbent baseline/tree. Every candidate remains a directed edge union rooted at `src`; reconstruct and validate a path to every destination before emitting paths for every partition.
Expected-gain check: this adds exact shared-trunk constructions unavailable to the incumbent’s all-terminal greedy ordering, and it is falsifiably beneficial only if hidden evaluation reports `combined_score > 0.00161523997524` for a configuration with more than seven distinct destinations.

strategies.title: [zero-cost-quotient-steiner] Contract free-transfer strongly connected regions b
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: zero-cost-quotient-steiner
Replacement scope: Replace the direct call to `_directed_steiner_edges(h, src, unique_dsts)` and its fixed `k > 7` cutoff with a quotient-and-expand exact-search phase.
Compute budget: One strongly-connected-components pass over the zero-cost subgraph, one quotient graph construction, and at most one exact DP over 10 quotient-terminal components; no optimizer starts or iterations. Expected evaluation-time effect: often lower than the current DP because the quotient has fewer nodes and may have fewer distinct terminal components.
Gain mechanism: Free directed links can create multiple equivalent ingress/egress points inside a cloud-region cluster. The incumbent treats those vertices independently, consuming DP state and forcing the low terminal-count cutoff even though travel within the cluster costs nothing. Form the subgraph of edges with cost exactly zero, contract each strongly connected component, retain the least-cost representative edge for every quotient arc, and map all destinations in a component to one quotient terminal. Solve the directed Steiner problem on that quotient. Expand every selected quotient arc to its original representative edge and add zero-cost directed paths inside each component from its entry point to every needed outgoing representative and terminal. Since SCC paths are directed and zero cost, expansion preserves reachability and the original monetary union cost exactly. Fall back to the original graph/tree if expansion cannot reach every terminal.
Expected-gain check: the quotient representation permits exact optimization over terminal groups that the incumbent cannot jointly optimize because they appear as separate terminals, and it is falsifiably beneficial only if it produces hidden `combined_score > 0.00161523997524` while preserving all destination-partition paths.

strategies.title: [partition-disjoint-striping] Assign partition paths over low-cost edge-diverse
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: partition-disjoint-striping
Replacement scope: Replace only the final loop that copies one identical `final_paths[dst]` route into every partition of `BroadCastTopology`.
Compute budget: For each unique destination, generate at most 4 loopless candidate paths using `nx.shortest_simple_paths`; perform at most `num_partitions × 4` deterministic candidate evaluations per destination. Expected evaluation-time effect: moderate only when several partitions are requested; no global exponential search.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent exposes no partition-level topology degree of freedom: every data partition traverses exactly the same route, even when the graph has independent low-cost alternatives. For each destination, retain the multicast-tree route plus up to three low-cost loopless alternatives. Assign partitions greedily by minimizing lexicographically `(incremental monetary edge cost, maximum accumulated inverse-throughput load, overlap with routes already assigned for that destination)`. The first partition always uses the selected multicast-tree route, preserving its shared broadcast behavior; alternative partitions are selected only from valid directed paths in `G`. This changes the output contact topology from a single serialized route to a stripeable multi-network bundle while retaining exactly one valid edge list for every `(dst, partition)`.
Expected-gain check: the incumbent cannot express distinct partition routes at all, so this is falsifiably beneficial precisely when a multi-partition configuration with alternate paths scores `combined_score > 0.00161523997524`.
